newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bonds ended slightly weaker on Thursday on the back of profit-taking as the market corrected after recent strength, traders said.
Government's benchmark R150 bond was last yielding 15.51 percent from an intraday best level of 15.43 percent and 15.49 percent late on Thursday.
The release of better-than-expected December trade figures had little effect on the market which had been expecting a positive number.
South Africa recorded a trade surplus of 2.040 billion rand in December from a 378 million rand surplus in November, latest South African Revenue Service figures showed.
"We saw quite a bit of profit-taking today which pushed the yield on the R150 above 15.50 percent...the market is seeing a bit of a correction after recent strength," a trader at a leading bank said.
The overall trend was still positive but moves appeared capped on the down- and upside as players started focusing on the options close-out on February 6.
"The guys are deciding how to get set on their options and this will put brakes on the market," the trader said.
Foreigners bought a net 80.67 million rands' worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after selling 42.32 million on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 9.20 billion rand on Wednesday from Tuesday's 4.81 billion rand, it said.
The rand ended firmer but off its best levels on the dollar following importer demand for the U.S. unit, forex traders said.
It ended at 4.6255/6305 on the dollar after strengthening to around 4.6140 during the morning, following upbeat comments by Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals on the currency.
The rand closed at 4.6300/6350 on the dollar on Wednesday.
"There was a bit of importer demand during the day which brought the rand back from its best levels," a trader at a foreign bank commented.
He said the unit had strengthened on the positive trade data but was unable to sustain gains.
Other traders said a test of the 4.60 level was on the cards early next week but felt the unit would first retrace to around 4.64.
Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank director of foreign exchange Willie Potgieter expected a more stable, long-term trend in the rand market barring any volatility on the political front.

On the crosses, the rand was last at 0.3547/3553 on the mark from 0.3535/3540 on Wednesday when it swept to a new six-month high. Against sterling it was at 7.5362/5453 from 7.6744/6873 after hitting a six-week high on Wednesday.
The Reserve Bank said South Africa's money market shortage fell to 10.048 billion rand on Wednesday from Tuesday's 10.664 billion rand.

Leading banks lowered their three-month NCD rates to a range between 17.25 and 17.40 percent from 17.25-17.50 percent while 90-day BA rates were also lower at 16.55-16.75 percent from 16.60-16.85 percent.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
